segments.text: Lionel Messi. Twenty-two years old, and already the world player of the year. The sixth of April, twenty ten. Camp Nou. A Champions League quarter-final, against Arsenal.
But first... we have to go back.
December, two thousand and nine. Messi wins the Ballon d'Or, by what was then a record margin.
Back at Camp Nou, Nicklas Bendtner scores in the eighteenth minute. Arsenal lead. What follows is a one-man show. By half-time, it reads: Messi three, Arsenal one.
One. Twenty-one minutes, from the edge of the box. Two. Thirty-seven, calmly past Almunia. Three. Forty-two, a chip over the keeper. Four. Eighty-eight, through his legs.
That season, he scored forty-seven goals, in fifty-three games. Thirty-four of them in La Liga.
Xavi said it best. A player like this only comes along every twenty-five to thirty years.
